reasoning: The package is a standard AUR packaging for the proprietary NVIDIA driver. The PKGBUILD downloads from the official NVIDIA domain, verifies checksums, and applies standard patches. All reviewed configuration, systemd, and udev files are benign and typical for this driver. The inconclusive verdict from qwen3-235b was due to an API error on a benign Xorg config file, not a security finding.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from an API error (HTTP 400) in the qwen3-235b model when processing nvidia-drm-outputclass.conf, forcing an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully processed the same file and correctly identified it as safe. The openrouter/free report is marked as advisory and also suffered from parsing errors, so it is excluded from the vote.
coverage_issues: Both qwen3-235b and deepseek-v4-flash incorrectly skipped '0001-Enable-atomic-kernel-modesetting-by-default.patch', misclassifying it as a binary file. Patch files are text and should be audited.
qwen3-235b failed to audit 'nvidia-drm-outputclass.conf' due to an LLM API error.
false_negatives: The skipped patch file '0001-Enable-atomic-kernel-modesetting-by-default.patch' was not reviewed for potential malicious code injection, though it is highly likely to be a standard upstream patch.
learnings: Fix file type detection: The tool incorrectly identifies .patch and .diff files as binary. These are text files and must be included in the audit context.
Implement retry logic or fallback for transient LLM API errors on individual files to prevent them from skewing the overall package verdict to inconclusive.
